Both are already linked to 188 common concepts, including functionally generated portfolio, scoring function and generating function, which suggests the methods and data needed to connect them already exist. We propose a study that uses functionally generated portfolio as a bridge: first, review how portfolio return and statistical arbitrage are each currently treated through functionally generated portfolio; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.
quant-3592-4519.phd: A 3-4 year programme building a unified framework for portfolio return and statistical arbitrage. Year 1: systematic review of the 188 shared concepts (starting with functionally generated portfolio, scoring function and generating function); years 2-3: develop and validate a joint method; year 4: generalise it and release open tools and data.
quant-3592-4519.masters: A 6-12 month project: reproduce one recent portfolio return study and one recent statistical arbitrage study, then run a focused experiment combining the two through functionally generated portfolio, reporting what transfers and what does not.

quant-2398-4182.title: Bridging investment portfolio and sample covariance matrix through esg score
quant-2398-4182.abstract: investment portfolio and sample covariance matrix are both active topics in Quant, yet no paper in our corpus has studied them together. Both are already linked to 75 common concepts, including esg score, volatility estimation and kelly criterion, which suggests the methods and data needed to connect them already exist. We propose a study that uses esg score as a bridge: first, review how investment portfolio and sample covariance matrix are each currently treated through esg score; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.
